title: القيادة والعمل الاحترافيّ
subtitle: The causative: have / get something done
intro: Professionals rarely say who did the work. They say the work got done. That is the causative — and it is the single grammar point that makes written English sound senior rather than junior.المحترفون نادراً ما يقولون من أنجز العمل، بل يقولون إنّ العمل أُنجز. هذا هو البناء السببيّ، وهو النقطة النحويّة التي تجعل إنجليزيّتك تبدو قياديّةً لا مبتدئة.
goals: I can use have/get something done accurately
I can delegate, instruct and report progress in English
I can run and summarise a professional meeting
I can hear the causative inside fast workplace speech

blocks.title: The core pattern
blocks.html:
have / get + object + past participle — someone else does it for you.

I had the report reviewed before the meeting.
→ I didn't review it. Someone did, because I arranged it.

Compare the three:
I reviewed the report. — me
I had the report reviewed. — someone else, I arranged it
The report was reviewed. — passive; nobody arranged anything

⚠️ The order is fixed: object before participle. I had reviewed the report is a past perfect — a completely different sentence.الترتيب ثابت: المفعول قبل التصريف الثالث. وانتبه: I had reviewed the report ماضٍ تامّ ومعنىً مختلفٌ تماماً.

blocks.title: have vs get — the difference that matters
blocks.html:
have something done — neutral, formal, standard business English
get something done — informal, and often implies effort or persuasion

We had the contract translated. — we arranged it
We finally got the contract translated. — it took work

get also carries the meaning of finishing:
Let's get it done by Friday. — the most common phrase in any office.have محايدة ورسميّة، وget غير رسميّة وتوحي بجهدٍ أو إلحاح. وget it done أشهر عبارةٍ في أيّ مكتب.

blocks.title: The unpleasant causative
blocks.html:
The same structure describes things you did not want:

She had her laptop stolen at the airport.
He had his proposal rejected twice.
They had their funding cut in March.

Nobody arranged these. The structure simply says: this happened to them. Context tells you which meaning is intended — there is no separate grammar.البناء نفسه يصف ما وقع عليك رغماً عنك. لا نحو مختلف — السياق وحده يفصل بين «رتّبتُ له» و«وقع عليّ».

blocks.title: Naming the person: have someone do
blocks.html:
When you want to say who:

I had the designer redo the slides. — have + person + bare infinitive
I got the designer to redo the slides. — get + person + to infinitive

One takes to, the other doesn't. This trips up almost everyone.

And for a service: I had someone look at it. — vague on purpose, very common.have + شخص + مصدرٌ مجرّد، وget + شخص + مصدرٌ بـto. فرقٌ دقيق يخطئ فيه الجميع تقريباً.

days.title: Reading: the manager who did everything
days.subtitle: نصّ + استنتاج المعنى من السياق

blocks.title: The Manager Who Did Everything
blocks.titleAr: المدير الذي كان يفعل كلّ شيء
blocks.en:
The most dangerous manager in any organisation is not the lazy one. It is the one who is excellent at the job below theirs. They write the code, fix the deck, rewrite the email, and every one of those tasks is done slightly better than the person who owns it would have done it. The work improves. The team stops growing.

Research on delegation has found the same pattern repeatedly. Teams whose managers had the work done by others, and then reviewed it, outperformed teams whose managers simply did the work — not immediately, but within about nine months. The first group looked slower at the start. It was not slower; it was building capacity while the second group was spending it.

The reason this mistake survives is that it feels like generosity. Taking a task off a tired colleague at eleven at night is genuinely kind. Doing it every week teaches them that their version will always be replaced, and eventually they stop trying to make it good.

The uncomfortable rule is that a manager's output is not what they produce. It is what their team can produce without them in the room. Anything that gets done only when you are present is not a system. It is a dependency, and it will fail on the first week you are ill.
blocks.ar:
أخطر مديرٍ في أيّ مؤسّسة ليس الكسول، بل البارع في الوظيفة التي تحته. فهو يكتب الشفرة، ويصلح العرض، ويعيد صياغة الرسالة، وكلّ مهمّةٍ من تلك تُنجَز أفضل قليلاً ممّا كان سيُنجزها صاحبها. يتحسّن العمل، ويتوقّف الفريق عن النموّ.

وقد وجدت الأبحاث في التفويض النمط نفسه مراراً. فالفرق التي جعل مديروها غيرهم ينجز العمل ثمّ راجعوه تفوّقت على الفرق التي أنجز مديروها العمل بأنفسهم — لا فوراً، بل خلال تسعة أشهرٍ تقريباً. بدت المجموعة الأولى أبطأ في البداية. ولم تكن أبطأ، بل كانت تبني قدرةً بينما كانت الثانية تستهلكها.

وسبب بقاء هذا الخطأ أنّه يبدو كرماً. فأخذ مهمّةٍ من زميلٍ منهَك في الحادية عشرة ليلاً لطفٌ حقيقيّ. لكنّ فعله كلّ أسبوعٍ يعلّمه أنّ نسخته ستُستبدَل دائماً، وينتهي به الأمر إلى التوقّف عن محاولة إتقانها.

والقاعدة غير المريحة أنّ ناتج المدير ليس ما يُنتجه هو، بل ما يستطيع فريقه إنتاجه وهو خارج الغرفة. وكلّ ما لا يُنجَز إلّا بحضورك ليس نظاماً، بل اعتماديّة، وستنهار في أوّل أسبوعٍ تمرض فيه.

days.title: Functional language and pronunciation
days.subtitle: Delegating, pushing back and reporting progress

blocks.title: Delegating without sounding like an order
blocks.html:
Direct: Do this by Friday. — rarely used between peers
Standard: Could you take the lead on this?
Softer: Would you be able to pick this up?
Softest: Is this something you'd have capacity for?
Handing over fully: I'd like you to own this end to end.

⚠️ own as a verb is everywhere in modern business English: Who owns this? = who is responsible.own فعلاً تعني «يتحمّل مسؤوليّة» في لغة الأعمال الحديثة: Who owns this؟ أي من المسؤول؟

blocks.title: Disagreeing with your manager, safely
blocks.html:
I see it slightly differently. — the standard opener
Can I offer a different read on that?
My concern would be that … — raises a risk without refusing
I'm happy to do it — I just want to flag the trade-off.
Help me understand the reasoning. — asks without challenging

Never: That's wrong. / I don't agree. as an opener. English softens the first move, then gets firm.الإنجليزية تليّن الخطوة الأولى ثمّ تشتدّ. لا تبدأ أبداً بـ«هذا خطأ» أو «لا أوافق».

blocks.title: 🚫 لا تقل هذا
blocks.html:
❌ I did my homework to the teacher → ✅ I had my homework checked
❌ I will do it done → ✅ I'll get it done
❌ Please do the needful → ✅ Please take care of it
❌ Kindly revert back to me → ✅ Please get back to me
❌ I am agree with you → ✅ I agree with you
❌ We discussed about the deadline → ✅ We discussed the deadline
❌ Explain me the process → ✅ Explain the process to me

do the needful and revert back are understood but mark you instantly as a non-native writer.«do the needful» و«revert back» مفهومتان لكنّهما تكشفان فوراً أنّك لست ناطقاً أصليّاً. وexplain تحتاج to me.

blocks.title: The task
blocks.prompt:
Write a progress update to a manager about a project that has slipped, in 130–150 words. It must include:

• two causatives (have / get something done)
• one get someone to do
• one sentence taking responsibility without excuses
• one clear ask with a deadline
• at least four words from this unitاكتب تحديثاً مهنيّاً لمديرك عن مشروعٍ تأخّر، في ١٣٠–١٥٠ كلمة، ببناءين سببيّين، وget someone to do، وجملةٍ تتحمّل فيها المسؤوليّة بلا أعذار، وطلبٍ واضحٍ بموعد، وأربع كلماتٍ من الوحدة.
phrases: We had the … reviewed / checked / approved …
The bottleneck turned out to be …
I should have escalated this sooner.
I couldn't get … to sign off on …
What I need from you is …
I'll circle back on Thursday with …
blocks.model:
Quick update on the migration.

The second milestone has slipped by nine days. We had the schema reviewed by the platform team and had the test data regenerated, and both came back clean, so the delay is not technical.

The bottleneck turned out to be sign-off. I couldn't get security to approve the access model, and it sat in their queue for two weeks. I should have escalated this on day three rather than waiting for a response. That one is on me.

What I need from you is a single decision: either we get the access model pre-approved for the remaining phases, or we reduce the scope and drop the audit log. I'd recommend the first.

I'll circle back on Thursday with a revised plan and a contingency for the supplier. No action needed before then.
blocks.modelAr:
تحديثٌ سريع عن مشروع الترحيل.

تأخّرت المحطّة الثانية تسعة أيّام. جعلنا فريق المنصّة يراجع المخطّط، وجعلنا بيانات الاختبار تُولَّد من جديد، وعاد الأمران بلا ملاحظات، فالتأخير إذن ليس تقنيّاً.

تبيّن أنّ عنق الزجاجة هو الاعتماد. لم أستطع أن أجعل فريق الأمن يوافق على نموذج الوصول، فبقي في طابورهم أسبوعين. وكان عليّ أن أرفع الأمر في اليوم الثالث بدل انتظار الردّ. هذه مسؤوليّتي أنا.

وما أحتاجه منك قرارٌ واحد: إمّا أن نجعل نموذج الوصول يُعتمد مسبقاً لبقيّة المراحل، وإمّا أن نقلّص النطاق ونُسقط سجلّ التدقيق. وأوصي بالأوّل.

سأعود إليك الخميس بخطّةٍ منقّحة وخطّةٍ بديلة للمورّد. ولا حاجة إلى أيّ إجراءٍ قبل ذلك.
checklist: I used 'have/get + object + past participle' at least twice
I used 'get someone to do' once, with 'to'
My object came before the participle (not 'I had reviewed the spec')
I took responsibility in one clear sentence, with no excuse attached
I made one specific ask with a date
I used at least four unit words (milestone, bottleneck, escalate, scope …)
I did not write 'revert back' or 'do the needful'
I closed with what happens next
